content: Every day, approximately 150,000 induced abortions are performed worldwide, amounting to 53 million annually, according to WHO data from 1997. Abortions during the first trimester can be carried out using either medical or surgical methods. Research has shown that a significant proportion of women, ranging from 64% to 90%, express a preference for medical abortion over surgical methods (Hill 1990; Tang 1991; Sun 1995). In the United States, around 670,000 women each year undergo abortions early enough in pregnancy to qualify for medical abortion methods (Kahn 2000). In China alone, over 15 million medical abortions have been performed in the past decade (Zhou 2002). Women have cited several reasons for choosing medical abortion, including the desire to avoid surgery, the perception of a more natural experience, the simplicity of the process, the privacy it offers, and the ability to undergo the procedure earlier in pregnancy (Creinin 1996). Additional factors influencing this choice include the less invasive nature of medical abortion, its ease of use, and the possibility of self-administration (Rosen 1979; Bachelot 1992; Sun 1995). However, medical abortion is associated with certain drawbacks compared to surgical abortion. It typically requires a longer duration to complete and is linked to greater blood loss (Chan 1993; Henshaw 1994; Winikoff 1996). The bleeding associated with medical abortion has been reported to last between 10 and 15 days (Peyron 1993; Spitz 1998). In some cases, the bleeding is severe enough to necessitate additional medical interventions, such as vacuum aspiration or dilatation and curettage (D&C), which occur in 0.8% of cases. Blood transfusions are required in approximately 0.1% of women undergoing medical abortion (Ulmann 1992). Excessive bleeding remains a significant concern for women undergoing medical abortion, and this issue has not yet been fully resolved. The underlying causes of heavy bleeding during medical abortion and the potential mechanisms by which Chinese medicinal herbs may help reduce bleeding warrant further investigation.
